subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the radical axis of the circles 2x² + 2y² + 3x + 6y − 5 = 0, 3x² + 3y² − 7x + 8y − 11 = 0.

mark_split.label: Write both circles in standard form
Subtract to find the radical axis

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write both circles in standard form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Divide by 2 and by 3 respectively before doing anything else.
lines: Given circles, divided to standard form:
steps.why: The radical axis formula S − S′ = 0 only cancels x² and y² correctly when both circles already carry coefficient 1 on those terms — dividing each circle by its own leading coefficient does this.
common_mistakes: Subtracting the two circles as originally printed, with leading coefficients 2 and 3, which gives a wrong line.
Dividing the x² term by the leading coefficient but forgetting to divide every other term the same way.
steps.memory_tip: Two different leading coefficients (2 and 3 here) is the signal to standardise BOTH circles before subtracting — never subtract un-standardised circles.

steps.label: Subtract to find the radical axis
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for the subtraction and the cleared final line.
steps.why: Subtracting the two standard-form circles cancels x² and y², leaving the radical axis; multiplying through by the common denominator 6 clears every fraction to give whole-number coefficients.
common_mistakes: Losing a sign while combining 3/2 and −(−7/3) into 23/6.
Leaving the final line with fractions instead of clearing it by the common denominator.
steps.memory_tip: Whenever the intermediate coefficients are fractions, multiply the whole final equation by their common denominator — here 6 — to reach the book's clean whole-number form.
